adjudicated.assessment: The source’s reflective “A beach outing... huh” contains no “then.” The added transition implies a conclusion not present.

adjudicated.jp: 「気にくわないこともあるだろうけど、明日から部活、来てみないか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I know you can't really stomach it, but couldn't you try coming to Club starting tomorrow?"
comments: "Stomach it" heee heee me so crubler- clevsder- cruller. Mmmh hungry nau. What were we talking about again? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source allows that there may be things she dislikes. “Can’t really stomach it” intensifies this into strong disgust.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “There may be things you don’t like, but why not try coming to club tomorrow?”

adjudicated.jp: 困惑と戸惑いを貼りつけて、彼女は伏していた顔をあげた。
adjudicated.en: Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment, she brought up her prostrate head.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says she lifts her downturned face with confusion and bewilderment written across it. “Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment” combines the emotions with each other, while “prostrate head” wrongly suggests full bodily prostration.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “Confusion and bewilderment on her face, she looked up.”

highlights.text: Gluing puzzlement to bewilderment, she brought up her prostrate head.

adjudicated.jp: 憔悴したその面差しが、緋色に色づけされてどこか悲壮な印象を与えた。
adjudicated.en: Her emaciated features turned a bright scarlet, and left me with an impression in some respects tragic.
adjudicated.assessment: 憔悴 describes a haggard or exhausted look, not physical emaciation. The English also awkwardly says the features themselves “left” an impression.
adjudicated.remedy: Use “Her haggard features flushed scarlet, giving her a strangely tragic look.”

highlights.text: Her emaciated features turned a bright scarlet, and left me with an impression in some respects tragic.
